review.theorem_assessment: Headline answers: the isotropic reading is correctly classified SOLVED-BY-PRIOR-WORK. Eq. (11) and Corollary 5 are both false as stated for arbitrary bases. No load-bearing defect was found. REVISE is only for minor text errors F1-F3. Thm 1: |c|=1 and division by component 1 give 1<=>2<=>3, and triangle equality with all w_j>0 gives 3<=>4<=>5. (T1), the disjoint-translate form, empty U and the co-array identity are correct. Zero weights reduce to the active subarray, and the one-sensor counterexample is right. Sec 3: G=H(+)L, ||x||>=2/||D|| on L, both sqrt2 examples and 2QZ^d in G are correct. Sec 4: S^{d-1}-S^{d-1}=2B_d (d>=2), Cor 2, the strict threshold, ULA 0<t<1, the endfire-only alias at t=1 and the open-interval case are correct. Thm 3: |d_j.x|<=2||d_j|| forces an integral k=Bx/2 with |k_i|<=floor||b_i||. Reconstruction plus residual integrality is sound and complete for (T3), on closed B_d/S^{d-1} only, as scoped. The rank-deficient branch is correct. Algebraic termination is sound: irreducible f makes a nonzero reduced residue nonzero at alpha, enclosures shrink, roots are simple, and there are no rational midpoints when deg f>=2. Lemma 4 holds in every n-case (|n|>=2 gives >=4b-a>=3a). (T5) is correct and equals Thm 3 with D=2V^{-1}. Sec 8: the minors argument, support agreement, Cauchy-Schwarz form and the |Z|<=1 / Z-empty split are correct. C alone falsifies Cor 5 under either reading (all vertex pairs, or vertices versus origin), Eq. (11) and the cell-coverage step. E shows Eq. (11) is strictly less stringent than Cor 5's test. The only-if directions of both remain trivially true.

independent_example_derivations.C: V^{-1}=[[1/3,-100/3],[0,10/3]], D matches and DV=2I. Via the unimodular map (m,n)->(m+10n,n), G={(3(m+10n),3n/10)}=3Z x (3/10)Z. lambda1=3/10, attained only at +-(0,3/10). Vertex differences up to sign (v1,v2,v1+v2,v2-v1): 9, 90009/100, 108909/100, 72909/100. The minimum 9 exceeds 4, and the binary sums are a subset, so Cor 5 and Eq. (11) both pass. x=10v1-v2=(0,-3/10), Dx=(20,-2). p2.u=(-200/3)(-3/20)=10 and p3.u=-1, so a(u)=(1,1,-1)=a(-u). V^{-1}(0,-3/10)=(10,-1) lies outside [-1,1]^2, so the origin-adjacent cells miss both shortest vectors. |u|=0.15 (about 8.6 deg from broadside; E about 9.1 deg), so no field-of-view or endpoint convention rescues either shortcut. 3D: D'=diag(D,2/3), G'=G x 3Z, and every added tested vector has squared norm >=9.

findings.issue: Successive shortest independent vectors need not give a basis or a point-free fundamental cell once r>=4. In Z^4+Z(1/2)(1,1,1,1), all 24 minimal vectors have norm 1, and e1..e4 realise every successive minimum but span an index-2 sublattice.
findings.required_change: Replace with a correct construction (inductively choose b_i in L cap span(a_1..a_i) with minimal positive a_i-coordinate) or cite one (e.g. Cassels, Ch. I). No result depends on it.

findings.issue: 'Circular' is misleading. For d<=4, Minkowski reduction is equivalent to finitely many explicit inequalities with coefficients in {0,+-1} (classical; cf. Nguyen-Stehle, ACM TALG 2009). These can be checked exactly. A basis passing them has b1 shortest, so both printed tests become valid in 3D, just as Gauss reduction validates them in 2D.
findings.required_change: State this accurately or delete the remark. (T5) remains an independent complete repair.

findings.location: Sec 4, 'reproduces the correct content of Tucker Prop 3/Cor 4'
findings.issue: The proof never fixes whether Tucker's D holds absolute positions or differences. With absolute positions and no sensor at the origin, Lambda={x: p_j.x in 2Z} can be a proper subgroup of G, and its norm test misses projective aliases. Example: d=1, p=(3/5,9/5) gives Lambda=(10/3)Z, which passes, but G=(5/3)Z and a(-5/6)=-a(5/6).
findings.required_change: Verify and state Tucker's convention, or qualify the reproduction claim. E and C are unaffected because p1=0 makes the two groups coincide.

findings.issue: The bound images page-0467..0469.png appear to match the JASA 70 pagination of Godara-Cantoni (pp. 467-475). The text never says what they show, yet it calls the theorem text inaccessible.
findings.required_change: Identify these images and reconcile them with the attribution paragraph.

findings.issue: The distinguishing-amplitude claim has no witness. The common-pattern reduction silently excludes zeros of h. No 3D sensor data are given.
findings.required_change: Add a witness, e.g. p=(0,1), u=1, v=-1, g1=1, g2(u)=2+u, giving b(1)=(1,-3) and b(-1)=(1,-1). Note that zeros of h are blind directions under the |Z|<=1 rule. List p4=(0,0,2/3).

review.prior_art_scope: Isotropic reading: SOLVED-BY-PRIOR-WORK is endorsed. The inspected primary support is Tucker Prop 3/Cor 4 for nontrivial full-rank lattices, subject to F3. Kastinen-Kero's normalized-inner-product ambiguity specialises to Thm 1 items 1 and 4 (uniform taper). Godara-Cantoni Thm 6 is secondary attribution only; its hypotheses and conventions are unverified. The extensions to rank-deficient, non-full-rank or trivial G and arbitrary U are routine linear algebra. Thm 3 and (T5) are standard bounded lattice enumeration with exact arithmetic: correct but not novel, as the proof says. The shortcut refutations are correct and NOVELTY-UNCLEAR pending an erratum search. That coefficient-bounded tests on unreduced bases miss shortest vectors is lattice folklore, so any novelty lies only in the specific correction. Directional/conformal reading: the exact criterion is prior or elementary, but there is no general decision procedure; the proof correctly does not claim it solved.
review.limitations: No tools were used: source content comes solely from the embedded quotes and summary. Hashes, page images, Tucker's conventions, the 1981 text and any erratum were not checked. Code and negative controls were not reviewed. All arithmetic was re-derived by hand. The F2 characterisation is cited from memory. Reviewer model: claude-opus-5-5 (Anthropic); the recorder must confirm whether this meets the 'other-vendor' requirement. This is not a formal verification.
